strengths: Identifies and clearly documents an underexplored problem: severe lack of per-prompt diversity in text-conditioned visual autoregressive (VAR) models, an issue that has been largely overshadowed by the community's focus on image quality/FID for these models.

Proposes a genuinely training-free, inference-only pipeline (noise injection into text embedding + scale-travel refinement) that requires no retraining or fine-tuning, making it practically appealing and easy to adopt.

The 'scale-travel' idea is a sensible and non-trivial adaptation of the diffusion 'time-travel'/resampling concept to the discrete, multi-scale autoregressive setting of VAR, exploiting the observation that early scales already encode coarse global structure -- a reasonable and moderately novel technical contribution.

Extensive empirical validation: two VAR backbones (Infinity, Switti), two datasets (MJHQ-30K, MS-COCO), multiple complementary metrics (LPIPS-MPD, Vendi score, FID, ImageReward), and Pareto-front analysis rather than single-point comparisons, which gives a more complete picture of the diversity-quality trade-off.

Rich supplementary material with ablations on noise schedulers, CFG weights, scale-travel hyperparameters (l, m), temperature/top-p sampling, text-alignment (GenEval, VQAScore), inference-time overhead, and comparison with prompt-rewriting, which strengthens reproducibility and shows the authors probed many alternative design choices.

Reported inference overhead is modest (~15-24%), supporting practical usability, and qualitative figures convincingly show that scale-travel removes visible artifacts introduced by condition annealing while retaining diversity.
weaknesses: The core technical novelty is somewhat incremental: the two main ingredients (CADS-style noise injection into conditioning and time-travel-like resampling) are directly imported from the diffusion literature; the contribution is primarily an adaptation/engineering exercise rather than a fundamentally new mechanism, which should temper claims of significance.

Only two VAR backbones are evaluated (Infinity and Switti), both fairly similar text-conditioned next-scale models; it remains unclear how well the method generalizes to other VAR variants or larger-scale models, limiting evidence for broad applicability.

Quality is not fully restored to the baseline level in several settings (e.g., Switti on MJHQ: FID rises from 16.18 to 21.34 with condition annealing and only partially recovers to 17.30 with scale-travel; ImageReward also remains below baseline in some configurations), indicating the 'sweet spot' still entails a non-trivial residual quality cost that is somewhat understated in the text.

Key hyperparameters (kmax for noise scheduling, and the scale-travel rewind points l and m) appear to be selected via manual grid search per backbone/dataset rather than a principled or automatic procedure, raising questions about how much tuning would be needed to deploy the method on a new model or prompt distribution.

Diversity is measured entirely through proxy statistics (LPIPS-MPD, Vendi, FID) without any human perceptual study on whether the generated diversity is meaningful/desirable, which is a common limitation but still leaves open whether the reported diversity gains correspond to genuinely useful variation versus noise-driven artifacts.

The paper acknowledges that even the most diverse configurations still exhibit visual artifacts in ~6% of samples, but this is only briefly mentioned as a limitation without deeper analysis of when/why these failures occur or how they might be mitigated further.

strengths: Identifies and clearly documents a genuine, previously under-examined limitation of text-conditioned VAR models (Infinity, Switti): severe lack of per-prompt diversity, illustrated convincingly in Fig. 1 and the additional qualitative panels.

The 'scale-travel' idea is a reasonably novel, domain-specific adaptation of the diffusion 'time-travel' trick to the multi-scale token structure of VAR, exploiting the multi-scale autoencoder to re-encode an accumulated feature map back to a coarser scale and resume generation—an interesting technical insight (Sec. 4.2, Fig. 3/4).

Experimental protocol is fairly thorough for a training-free method: two VAR backbones (Infinity, Switti), two datasets (MJHQ-30K, MS-COCO), four complementary metrics (FID, ImageReward, LPIPS-MPD, Vendi score), and full Pareto-front sweeps over hyperparameters for every baseline technique compared (CFG scheduling, two condition-annealing variants), which is a more rigorous comparison protocol than a single-operating-point table.

Extensive supplementary ablations (scheduler choice, scale-travel start/target stages, temperature/top-p sampling, GenEval/VQAScore text alignment, comparison with prompt-rewriting, inference-time overhead) support reproducibility and show the authors probed many alternative design choices.
The method is training-free and reports only modest inference overhead (~15–24%), which is practically appealing since it requires no retraining or fine-tuning of the underlying VAR model.
Clear writing and figures; pseudocode (Algorithms 1–2) and explicit formulas make the core scale-travel mechanism reproducible.
weaknesses: Core novelty is limited: the diversity-inducing component is essentially a direct import of CADS-style text-embedding noise injection from diffusion models with no VAR-specific modification (Sec. 4.1), and the CFG-scheduling comparison is likewise a straightforward transplant of existing diffusion scheduling literature. The paper's genuinely new piece is confined to the scale-travel refinement, making the overall contribution more of an adaptation/engineering exercise than a substantial new algorithmic idea.

The abstract's claim of 'significant diversity gains with minimal quality degradation' is not fully supported by Table 1: for Switti on MJHQ-30K, FID actually worsens from 16.18 (baseline) to 17.30 with scale-travel, and ImageReward drops from 1.11 to 0.93 (~16% relative degradation)—these are not clearly 'minimal' and the method does not recover baseline quality, only partially mitigates the degradation introduced by noise injection.

No human perceptual study is included despite the paper's central claim being about a subjective quality/diversity trade-off; reliance solely on automated proxies (ImageReward, FID, LPIPS, Vendi) is a meaningful limitation for a paper about perceptual diversity and artifact correction.

Only two VAR backbones are tested, both fairly similar next-scale prediction architectures (Infinity and Switti); it remains unclear whether the scale-travel mechanism generalizes to other VAR variants (e.g., FlexVAR, M-VAR, or masked/other multi-scale designs) or depends on specific properties of the particular multi-scale VQ-VAE used.

The scale-travel procedure itself introduces an additional lossy re-encoding/decoding round-trip through the multi-scale autoencoder, and the paper's own limitations note that ~6% of the most diverse outputs still show visual artifacts—suggesting the trade-off is only partially resolved rather than eliminated.

Hyperparameter selection (target scale m, noise schedule, k_max) appears tuned per-model/per-dataset via a 'toy experiment' rather than a principled or automatic procedure, raising concerns about sensitivity and practical deployment without such tuning.

The Pareto-front figures (Fig. 6) are the primary quantitative evidence of the claimed dominance, but curve interpolation/comparison across differently-parameterized methods can be visually persuasive while masking cases (as in Table 1) where the operating point actually used underperforms the baseline on quality; a clearer, single fair operating-point comparison would strengthen the claims.

strengths: Identifies and clearly documents an important but previously overlooked problem: text-conditioned VAR models (e.g., Infinity, Switti) exhibit severe lack of per-prompt diversity, filling a gap since prior diversity-enhancement work has focused almost exclusively on diffusion models.

The proposed scale-travel technique is a well-motivated, architecture-aware adaptation of the diffusion 'time-travel' idea to VAR's multi-scale token structure, exploiting the fact that VAR's multi-scale autoencoder can re-encode an accumulated feature map to approximately 'revert' to a coarser scale — a non-trivial technical insight given that VAR's autoregressive generation cannot be reversed like diffusion's stochastic process.

Thorough empirical evaluation: Pareto-front analysis across two datasets (MJHQ-30K, MS-COCO) and two VAR backbones (Infinity, Switti), multiple quality/diversity metrics (LPIPS-MPD, Vendi, ImageReward, FID), and consistent framing of results as Pareto trade-offs rather than single-point comparisons.

Extensive ablations in the supplementary material (CFG/annealing scheduler choices, scale-travel start/end stage selection, temperature and top-p sampling, text-alignment via GenEval and VQAScore, prompt-rewriting comparison) that substantially strengthen the empirical case and reproducibility.
Practical benefit: the method is training-free and adds only modest inference overhead (~15-24%), and the paper reports this cost transparently.

Qualitative figures across many diverse prompts (including main paper and extensive supplementary galleries) convincingly show that condition-annealing introduces diversity but with visible artifacts, and that scale-travel largely repairs these artifacts while retaining diversity.
The paper is transparent about limitations, explicitly reporting that ~6% of generated samples still contain visual artifacts and that scale-travel introduces some inference overhead.
weaknesses: The core technical novelty is somewhat incremental: the two diversity-enhancement techniques explored (CFG scheduling, condition-annealing/noise injection) are directly imported from prior diffusion literature (CADS, dynamic CFG), and the paper's own new component (scale-travel) is a relatively simple analogy applied to an existing architectural mechanism (multi-scale encoding) already used in VAR; the conceptual leap, while sound, is modest.

Quantitative results are mixed relative to the un-modified baseline model: for example, Switti's FID after the full DiverseVAR pipeline (17.30 on MJHQ-30K) is worse than the plain baseline (16.18), and ImageReward for Switti drops from 1.11 (baseline) to 0.93 (DiverseVAR), indicating the method does not fully preserve baseline quality even after refinement — this is acknowledged as a trade-off but somewhat understates the residual quality cost in the main narrative.

Evaluation is limited to two VAR backbones (Infinity and Switti), both from a similar 'next-scale' family; it remains unclear how well the scale-travel idea generalizes to other emerging VAR variants (e.g., FlexVAR, M-VAR) or to VAR models lacking an explicit reusable multi-scale autoencoder, which is a structural prerequisite for the method.

The Pareto-front figures (Fig. 6) are visually dense with many overlapping curves, making precise quantitative comparison difficult from the plots alone; the paper relies on the reader trusting the qualitative 'DiverseVAR sets the frontier' claim without, e.g., area-under-curve or other summary statistics to make the frontier comparison rigorous.

No user study or human evaluation is included to validate that the perceived quality/diversity trade-off aligns with human judgment, relying instead on automated proxy metrics (ImageReward, FID, LPIPS, Vendi) that can have known biases.

The choice of scale-travel start/end stages (l, m) appears to require per-model tuning (different values for Infinity vs. Switti), suggesting the method's optimal operating point may not transfer easily to new models or datasets without additional hyperparameter search.

strengths: Identifies and clearly demonstrates an important, previously under-examined problem: severe lack of per-prompt output diversity in text-conditioned VAR models, which had been overshadowed by focus on quality/speed.

Systematic, well-motivated exploration of diversity-enhancement techniques (CFG scheduling vs. condition-annealing) adapted from diffusion literature to the VAR setting, with clear empirical justification for choosing text-embedding noise injection.

The proposed scale-travel mechanism is a genuinely novel, non-trivial adaptation of latent 'rewind-and-refine' editing ideas to the scale-wise (rather than temporal/diffusion-step) axis of VAR, exploiting the multi-scale encoder in an elegant way (Algorithm 1 vs 2 comparison is clear).

Extensive experiments across two image VAR backbones (Infinity, Switti), a video VAR (InfinityStar), and even class-conditioned VAR, with multiple diversity/quality metrics (LPIPS-MPD, Vendi, ImageReward, FID, VBench) consistently showing DiverseVAR sits on the Pareto frontier.

Thorough ablations in the appendix: scheduler choices, scale-travel target parameters, robustness to CFG/temperature/nucleus sampling, comparison with prompt rewriting and fine-tuning-based diversity methods (CSD-VAR, Kaleido), scalability across model sizes/resolutions, and inference-time overhead analysis (only ~15-24% slower).
Training-free, plug-and-play nature increases practical impact and ease of adoption; reasonably reproducible given the detailed hyperparameter settings provided in the supplementary.
Honest limitations section acknowledging residual artifacts (~6% of samples) and modest inference overhead rather than overselling the method.
weaknesses: The core techniques (CADS-style noise injection, CFG scheduling, SDEdit/inpainting-style rewind-refine) are all adapted from prior diffusion-model literature; the primary novelty is the scale-travel adaptation to VAR's discrete multi-scale structure, which is a comparatively narrow (though non-trivial) engineering contribution rather than a fundamentally new algorithmic idea.

Diversity gains still come with a non-trivial, if reduced, quality cost and a measurable inference-time overhead (up to 24%), and per the limitations section ~6% of outputs still show visible artifacts, so the trade-off is improved but not fully resolved.

Optimal hyperparameters for scale-travel (target scale m, kmax, scheduler type) appear to require per-model/per-dataset tuning based on a 'toy experiment' (Sec 5.3), and although a wide grid is explored, no principled or automatic way to select these parameters at test time is provided.

Text-alignment/quality metrics (VQAScore, GenEval, IR) uniformly show slight degradation versus baseline; while argued to be a natural byproduct of increased diversity, the paper could more rigorously quantify how much of this is an intrinsic diversity-quality trade-off versus an artifact of the method itself.

Diversity metrics used (LPIPS-MPD, Vendi) primarily capture pixel/perceptual variation and may not fully capture semantic diversity or degenerate 'diversity' from artifacts; a human study or perceptual quality study would strengthen the quality claims beyond automated metrics like ImageReward/FID.

Comparisons with CADS-style baselines and CFG scheduling are reimplemented within the VAR setting by the authors themselves (since no prior VAR diversity work exists), so there is some risk that baseline configurations are not fully optimized, potentially inflating DiverseVAR's relative advantage in Fig. 6.
